title: Expectations catch up

predict.q: Same rule as before: inflation = expected inflation + (5 − U), and people expect last year's inflation. This time unemployment is held at 4% for three years. What happens to inflation?

options.s: It stays at 3%: the economy has picked its point on the curve
options.fb: That is only year 1. Next year people expect 3%, so the SRPC shifts up.

options.s: It rises every year: 3%, then 4%, then 5%
options.fb: Each year expectations catch up with last year's inflation and the SRPC shifts up: 3%, 4%, 5%.

options.s: It returns to 2% once people get used to it
options.fb: Expectations catch up with actual inflation, not with the old 2%. Inflation keeps rising.

options.s: It falls, because unemployment is low
options.fb: Unemployment below the natural rate pushes inflation up, not down.

task: Set the unemployment slider to 4%, then move the year slider from 0 to 3. Watch the SRPC shift.

target.do: Set unemployment to 4%, then move the year slider to 3, then press Check.

takeaway: With adaptive expectations, the trade-off lasts only until expectations catch up.
